subject: Next steps: Finway delete/retention & backup QA
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reed <tom.reed@finway.com>
Cc: privacy@finway.com
Date: Thu, 3 Oct 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: RTBF & deletion items from today's call

Tom — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the security/privacy review moving: 

- Scope: Finway will need confirmed deletion for user-level PII and model-derived user artifacts for accounts that request RTBF.
- Backups: you asked about timing for removing data from snapshots and long-term backups.
- Logs: need to know what logs are retained for troubleshooting and whether they can be redacted for identified users.
- Residency: all deletion actions must execute in the us-east region and we should confirm snapshot replication windows.

Attachments: I attached a simple snapshot matrix and a one-pager diagram of our erase pipeline. See the attached files (finway-rtbf-snapshot-matrix.xlsx, redwood-erase-diagram.png).

Proposed next steps:
1) Please confirm the specific PII fields you require us to consider part of the RTBF (email, SSN, payment tokens, or custom identifiers).
2) If you can share a redline or bullet list of any additional legal constraints (Elena, copying you) we’ll route to privacy engineering.
3) I’ll loop in Karthik and Vivek for the technical timelines (backups/snapshots).

Can you confirm availability for a 30-min follow up tomorrow afternoon?

Thanks,

—Marissa

From: Tom Reed <tom.reed@finway.com>

Cc: Elena Santos <elena.santos@finway.com>, privacy@finway.com
Date: Thu, 3 Oct 2029 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: RTBF & deletion items from today's call

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few clarifications from Finway's side: 

1) PII scope: primary identifier is customer_email (we also need to cover last4 payment tokens, billing_address, and any KYC identifiers ingested). We will provide a full data dictionary by EOD.
2) Backups: our legal team requires that recoverable backups containing a user's PII be purged within 90 days of a verified delete request, or a contractual commitment that backups be overwritten and unrecoverable.
3) Snapshots: we need a statement of how long point-in-time snapshots are retained and whether snapshots are replicated across regions.
4) Logs: application and request logs are acceptable for troubleshooting, but they must be retained in anonymized form after the delete. We need an ability to request a scrub/redaction for specific identifiers.
5) Audit evidence: we will require a machine-readable proof-of-deletion report (timestamped, signed by KMS key ID used) for each verified RTBF.

Also copying Elena for any legal comments. Can Karthik confirm feasibility on the 90-day backup purge and on-snapshot replication? Vivek, any concerns on signed proofs?

Tom Reed
Director, Security & Privacy
Finway Inc.
tom.reed@finway.com | +1 212-555-0987

Appreciate the detail, Tom — that helps. Quick plan from our side: 

- Karthik, can you confirm the default retention windows and whether we can commit to a 90-day backup purge (or provide an overwrite + attest model)?
- Vivek, can your team produce the machine-readable proof-of-deletion artifacts that include a timestamp and KMS key ID? If we can produce a signed hash/proof we’ll include that in the audit report.
- Marissa (me) will collect the Finway data dictionary once received and map fields to our internal retention labels so we can scope deletions precisely.

Tom/Elena — a couple of quick clarifying questions for your legal/security teams so we can provide an accurate contract clause: 
1) Is 90 days an absolute contractual deadline, or is a technical attestation of irreversible overwrite acceptable if done earlier than 90 days?
2) For the machine-readable proof, do you have a preferred format (JSON-LD, signed CSV, or other)?

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
- Today: Finway shares data dictionary + any redline legal bullets (Tom/Elena).
- Tomorrow: 30-min technical sync with Karthik/Vivek to walk through backup topology and proof format.
- Within 5 business days after sync: Redwood will provide a draft contract appendix language + a sample proof-of-deletion JSON.

If that looks good, I’ll book the 30-min slot for tomorrow 2:00–2:30pm PT. 

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@finway.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Elena Santos <elena.santos@finway.com>, privacy@finway.com
Date: Fri, 4 Oct 2029 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Follow-up: RTBF & deletion items from today's call

Hi all — thanks for the context. Technical notes and feasibility summary below (high level; we can expand in tomorrow's sync):

1) PII mapping: once we receive Finway's data dictionary we will map the fields into three internal retention categories: immediate-delete (user PII + model index entries), session-ephemeral (short-term traces), and long-term-audit (anonymized event aggregates). We can provide the mapping artifact.

2) Backups & snapshots:
   - Our production snapshots are taken every 6 hours and retained for 30 days in the primary region (us-east-1). Snapshot replication to a secondary region is configured for DR but can be disabled per-customer for Private/Dedicated customers; hosted accounts currently replicate to us-west for DR.
   - For hosted Finway account: we can commit to making PII unrecoverable in backups within 90 days by applying an overwrite-and-garbage-collect process. Practically, the timeline is: mark objects for deletion immediately, initiate an overwrite of affected objects in object storage (multi-pass overwrite), then allow storage provider lifecycle policies to finalize. We estimate that for most requests this results in irreversible removal within 7–21 days for object storage but full guarantee across snapshot chains requires up to 90 days.
   - For stronger contractual wording we can offer an alternative: a contractual attestation that we performed a cryptographic shred (replace key + re-encrypt) where applicable, plus a certified overwrite of snapshots when customer has Dedicated or Private deployment.

3) Proof-of-deletion (machine-readable):
   - We can produce a signed JSON report per request with: request_id, user_identifier_hash (SHA256), deletion_timestamp (ISO8601), affected_artifacts list, KMS_key_id, and signature (RSA/ECDSA over the report). Sample JSON schema will be provided.

4) Logs & redaction:
   - Request/application logs are retained for 90 days by default. We can offer a per-request scrub request where our ops team redacts matching identifiers (we'll need exact match keys or regexes). Redaction is supported for request logs and request payload traces; system-level audit logs that feed billing are retained in anonymized form only.

5) Action items/risks:
   - We should confirm whether snapshot replication must be disabled (it affects the 90-day window).
   - If Finway requires a shorter backup purge than 90 days for hosted accounts, we should discuss Dedicated/Private deployment or a contractual attestation + additional fee.

I can join tomorrow's 2:00pm PT slot — I’ll bring a short slide that diagrams our snapshot lifecycle and a sample signed-proof payload. Vivek can speak to KMS signing details.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Privacy Engineer | Redwood Inference
